summary.text: Brad Thomas is a Republican state representative who has represented Georgia House District 21 since January 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Anthony Aragues Jr.
A U.S. Navy veteran with a degree in mechanical engineering technology, he has worked as an engineer for the U.S. Department of Energy and owns a business.

paragraphs.text: Thomas graduated from Dunwoody High School, served in the U.S. Navy and reached the rank of petty officer second class, and earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering technology from Georgia Southern University.
His career experience includes working as an engineer with the U.S. Department of Energy and owning a business.
Thomas won the 2020 Republican primary for House District 21, defeating Rajpal Sagoo in the primary and Bill Fincher in the August 11 runoff, and then defeated William Hughes in the general election.
He was re-elected in 2022 and defeated Mitchell Simmons in the 2024 general election.

For the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to eight committees, including Defense and Veterans Affairs, Energy, Utilities and Telecommunications, and Transportation, serving as vice chair of Governmental Affairs and of Technology and Infrastructure Innovation and as chair of the Special Committee on Resource Management.

In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a principled conservative and said his key messages were putting Cherokee County and Georgia first, responsible growth in Cherokee County, and opposing the growth of government.
